facility_roles.quote: The G0 experiment in Hall C at the Thomas Jefferson National Accelerator Facility (Jefferson Lab) in Newport News, VA utilizes a specialized apparatus
we have provided a description of the polarized electron beam produced by the CEBAF accelerator

intervals.label: installation and commissioning runs (first installed July-October 2002, reinstalled autumn 2003)
intervals.note: The experiment was installed July-October 2002 and followed by a first commissioning run of about three months, then reinstalled in the autumn of 2003 with another commissioning/engineering run; it was not continuously installed in between. The end is the start of forward-angle production ('about mid-March 2004').
intervals.quote: The G0 experiment was first installed in Hall C of Jefferson Lab during the period July 2002 to October 2002.

intervals.label: forward-angle production run (about March-May 2004)
intervals.note: Production stopped when the statistical goals of the forward-angle measurement had been met.
intervals.quote: The actual production runs for the forward angle measurement began about mid-March 2004 and continued until about May 2004

intervals.label: installation of the backward-angle hardware
intervals.note: Start is the end of the forward-angle run; end is the start of backward-angle commissioning ('March to May of 2006'). The installation itself is not dated in the source.
intervals.quote: Having completed the forward angle measurement, the new hardware for the back angle measurements was installed in Hall C, and commissioning and initial data-taking took place in March to May of 2006.

intervals.label: backward-angle commissioning and production (March 2006 to April 2007)
intervals.note: Hydrogen and deuterium targets, each at 359 and 684 MeV; commissioning and initial data-taking in March-May 2006 followed by a long production period.
intervals.quote: A long period of production running followed – including measurements with both hydrogen and deuterium targets, each at beam energies of 359 and 684 MeV – ending in April 2007.

intervals.label: completed
intervals.note: The end of production running (April 2007) is the last documented G0 data taking; the source does not use the word 'completed'.
intervals.quote: A long period of production running followed – including measurements with both hydrogen and deuterium targets, each at beam energies of 359 and 684 MeV – ending in April 2007.

name: G0
notes: No website: the G0 collaboration page linked from the HAPPEX site (www.npl.illinois.edu/exp/G0/G0Main.html) returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-26.

Dates come from the operation history in the G0 apparatus paper (arXiv:1103.0761, section 8): installation July-October 2002, forward-angle production about mid-March to May 2004, backward-angle commissioning March-May 2006, production ending April 2007. The upgrade interval (new backward-angle hardware) is bounded by those dates, not separately dated.

The 2005 forward-angle paper reported non-zero strange-quark contributions; the later HAPPEX-III result found the combined world data consistent with zero (see result:happex-iii-strange-vector-form-factors-2011).

physics_goals.quote: the parity-violating elastic scattering of electrons from protons and quasi-elastic scattering from deuterons is measured in order to determine the neutral weak currents of the nucleon
physics_goals.value: Measure the neutral weak currents of the nucleon, and from them the strange-quark contribution to its form factors, by parity-violating elastic electron scattering from protons and quasi-elastic scattering from deuterons

summary.plain: G0 used a large superconducting magnet in Hall C of Jefferson Lab to catch particles scattered from hydrogen and deuterium by a spin-flipping electron beam. The tiny differences between the two spin states map the strange quarks' contribution to the proton's charge and magnetism across a range of momentum transfers.
summary.technical: Parity-violating electron scattering with a superconducting toroidal magnetic spectrometer in Hall C: forward-angle running (3 GeV beam, recoil protons detected by time of flight, 0.12 < Q^2 < 1.0 GeV^2; production March to May 2004) and backward-angle running on hydrogen and deuterium (359 and 684 MeV, Q^2 = 0.22 and 0.63 GeV^2; March 2006 to April 2007), separating the strange electric and magnetic form factors and the nucleon's axial form factor (anapole effects).
